content: 1. Khan A. explored the perspectives of healthcare providers on the management of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in Pakistan. This study was published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association in 2012, volume 62, issue 9, pages 941-945. 2. Iipinge SN and Pretorius L. examined the delivery and quality of STI treatment provided by private general practitioners in Windhoek, Namibia. Their findings were published in the Global Journal of Health Science in 2012, volume 4, issue 5, pages 156-171. 3. Weaver MR, Pillay E, Jed SL, De Kadt J, Galagan S, Gilvydis J, and colleagues conducted a pilot study comparing three methods of delivering clinic-based training on syndromic management of STIs in South Africa. The results were published in the journal Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2016, volume 92, issue 2, pages 135-141. 4. Hoffman CM, Fritz L, Matlakala N, Mbambazela N, Railton JP, McIntyre JA, and others investigated community-based strategies to identify unmet care needs for individuals with STI-associated symptoms in rural South Africa. Their study appeared in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2019, volume 24, issue 8, pages 987-993. 5. Aaron K, Jordan S, Schwebke J, Van Der Pol B, and Hook E studied the continuation of sexual activity among men after the onset of urethritis symptoms. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2018, volume 45, Supplement 2, page S38. 6. Ham DC, Hariri S, Kamb M, Mark J, Ilunga R, Forhan S, and colleagues evaluated the quality of STI case management services in Gauteng Province, South Africa, focusing on healthcare providers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2016, volume 43, issue 1, pages 23-29. 7. Alemayehu A and Godana W assessed the knowledge and practices of clinicians regarding syndromic management of STIs in public health facilities in the Gamo Gofa Zone, South Ethiopia. Their research was published in the Journal of Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2015, article ID 310409. 8. Hussain MF, Khanani MR, Siddiqui SE, Manzar N, Raza S, and Qamar S investigated the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of general practitioners in Karachi, Pakistan, regarding STIs and HIV/AIDS. Their findings were published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association in 2011, volume 61, issue 2, pages 202-205. 9. Adhikari LM, Thapa SB, Sherchan L, and Adhikari C evaluated the effectiveness of syndromic STI case management and reproductive health training in improving the knowledge and practices of auxiliary health workers. This study was published in the Journal of Universal College of Medical Sciences in 2014, volume 2, issue 3, pages 34-37. 10. Garcia PJ, Carcamo CP, Garnett GP, Campos PE, and Holmes KK reported on improved STI syndrome management through a network of clinicians and pharmacy workers in Peru, known as the PREVEN Network. Their study was published in PLoS ONE in 2012, volume 7, issue 10. 11. Korenromp EL, Wi T, Resch S, Stover J, and Broutet N analyzed the costs of implementing national STI programs as part of the global STI control strategy for the health sector (2016–2021). Their findings were published in PLoS ONE in 2017, volume 12, issue 1.
